checked_without_candidate: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 Tournament.sol: I traced every state change that can delete, eliminate or re-pair a commitment (joinTournament, pairCommitment, advanceMatch, sealLeafMatch, winLeafMatch, sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament, winInnerTournament, eliminateInnerTournament, winMatchByTimeout, eliminateMatchByTimeout, deleteMatch). deleteMatch with WinnerCommitment.NONE is reached only from ELIMINATE_BOTH (which needs both clocks expired, or the paused survivor's remainder used up by the responder's overdue time, i.e. the survivor did not act within its own clock) or from an ELIMINABLE child. A child is ELIMINABLE only when no dangling winner is left or the winner's window resultAt+allowance has passed. If the honest inner commitment joined, it is always the last survivor (every winner re-pairs with the dangling commitment), so the window runs on the honest commitment's own clock.

Commitment identity: Clock.initializePausedAt -> requireUninitialized lets a root join each tournament only once. An adversary that front-runs the honest join with the same root can only join earlier, and the late-join deduction then leaves the honest clock at least as much time. Adversary moves on behalf of the honest commitment (advance, seal, win) reveal nodes that the hash fixes, and they charge the honest clock no more than its own move would.

Match bisection invariant (Match.create/advanceBisection/sealDivergence): the revealing parent never equals the waiting parent, so the two sealed final states always differ. The agreed state is proved only against the revealing commitment at leaf p-1, and it equals the waiting commitment's leaf p-1: it is either the equal left leaf, or the last leaf of a left subtree compared equal at the most recent right turn, or the initialHash at p=0. finalStateOne/Two are mapped to the commitment ids by height parity. instantiateInner pairs contestedCommitmentOne with finalStateOne. winInnerTournament derives the parent commitment from the winner's final state alone, so an inner claim that ends at the honest state can only help the honest outer claim.

Match-id reuse: pairCommitment runs before deleteMatch in every win path. A new match (dangling, winner) cannot hash to the deleted (one, two), because a commitment in a live match is never dangling at the same time.

Orphan child tournaments: matchIdFromInnerTournaments is written only by sealing and cleared on win or elimination. An unregistered child maps to a zero id that does not exist, so requireSealed reverts. A sealed inner match keeps both clocks paused, so it can be deleted only through its child.

CartesiStateTransition + DaveConsensus.provideMerkleRootOfInput: the honest leaf proof is checked against InputBox hashes of the current epoch. The earlier note that the provider reads the current epoch's bounds is harmless: a root reaches ROOT_WINNER only with matchCount==0, so every registered child is already resolved before the next seal.

PRT referee model (doc/recipes/prt.lua, game-transport.lua): new_match/advance_bisection/validate_seal_response/settle_divergence/open_uarch_tournament/partition_claims agree with Dave on who wins. Uarch claims must end at a contested state, and the winner's final state picks the mcycle claim. Of the model's leaf-race and propagation differences from Dave (proofs accepted until the later deadline, no winner expiry), both are simplifications the manual itself lists (doc/README.md near line 11308), so they are not normative.

Length confusion in model proofs: the JSON schemas decode target_hash, sibling_hashes and node fields as Base64 of any length. But cartesi.keccak256 with two arguments refuses inputs that are not 32 bytes (clua-cartesi.cpp cartesi_mod_hasher), so a 64-byte target with an empty sibling cannot pass verify_slice and authenticate an inner node as a leaf. The same holds for the 'keccak(left,right)' checks in validate_claim_response, validate_bisection_response and validate_seal_response.

Subscription namespaces in the model (keccak(tid, claim) with uarch tid = keccak(c1,c2)): a collision with the mcycle namespace would need an mcycle claim whose computation hash equals the initial machine hash, together with a 62-level final-leaf proof. That proof would have to go below the machine tree's 32-byte word leaves, which hash 32 bytes rather than 64, so it cannot be built.

PRT bridge (support) job derivation: responder parity at creation and at seal (H=54 and H=38, so commitment two seals), the winLeafMatch window [0,min(d1,d2)) and the winMatchByTimeout window [min, eliminableAt), the winInnerTournament binding through holds(parent, parentCommitment), and the epoch listener's split of inputs by (blockNumber, logIndex) at EpochSealed, which matches DaveConsensus sampling the InputBox inside the acceptance transaction.
not_covered: No experiment was run on the local chain with the pinned Dave contracts or on the EVM harness. Everything above is from reading code (Tournament.sol, Match.sol, MatchClocks.sol, Clock.sol, Commitment.sol, Tree.sol, Time.sol, MultiLevelTournamentFactory.sol, CartesiStateTransition.sol, DaveConsensus.sol, prt.lua referee and player handlers, game-transport.lua request semantics, prt-bridge.lua observe/update_claims/jobs/prepare, prt-epoch.lua).

Eliminations that need a timeout of the honest claim, which this angle excludes. Whether the released clocks (maxAllowance = censorship + 2*response + refill, COMMITMENT_BUDGET 120 min) leave the honest root join and the leaf-race proof enough time. In particular, the PRT player joins the root only after it sees EpochSealed under the 'finalized' input policy, and the late-join deduction charges that delay to the honest root clock (A7, noted as uncovered in R3 VARSCHED, not analysed here).

Completeness failures that would make the honest leaf proof or the honest inner join fail (an uarch claim final state that differs from the mcycle leaf at a period end, rejection or fixed-point leaves, step-verifier acceptance). These are R2/R4/R6 territory and earlier rounds covered them.
Bond, refund and gas economics: whether adversary-forced matches can drain the honest signer below a join bond, so that the honest inner commitment cannot join.
The number of sequential matches that asynchronous pairing lets a Sybil population force on the honest claim (prt-delay-bound.md not read).
Output validation (A5) and the rollups-contracts Application/executeOutput path.
Dave docs/reviews and the Rust node: not read (blind hunt; out of scope).
